review: legion-worker: the merge-gate and review-threads references govern the review of this multi-package PR against plan.md's site list

summary: Every test-started server gets its port as a socket the harness opened on port 0 and hands over (DISPATCH_LISTEN_FD, ENVOY_LISTEN_FD, LEGION_LISTEN_FD, shared envoy/listenfd package), or binds port 0 itself and reports it. FreeTCPPort, freePorts, boundPort and free-port.sh are deleted, along with every fixed default in the named harnesses, and explicit overrides are used as given. One PR in three phases: the mechanism, the Envoy tests in the spec, then the sites the architect added.
phases: 1: packages/envoy/listenfd; envoy-dispatch DISPATCH_LISTEN_FD; envoy-listener ENVOY_LISTEN_FD and its bound-address log; legion start LEGION_LISTEN_FD; cmdtest.HoldPort replaces FreeTCPPort

2: dispatch/listener launchers, memory harness, infra/core natslive launchers, infra/host held-port wrapper image and envoy-smoke step, scripts/e2e/lib/held-port.py with its test, listener-deploy-probe, e2e-local, search-smoke and searchbench

3: daemon scratch-Dispatch test, claude-envoy smoke, Dispatch Playwright harness (harness-start.ts, e2e/run.ts wrapper, fakes report their bound ports, local-instance, docs harness), scripts/e2e rig.sh (start_held, keep_port, start_kept), every stage script, bridge-tunnel, docs rigs, skill-scenarios rig; free-port.sh deleted

acceptance.surface: repository grep; pod Go tests (listenfd, cmdtest, cmd/listener, cmd/dispatch with Job Postgres, daemon); bun test scripts/e2e/lib/held-port.test.ts; go test ./host/heldportwrapper/; e2e-local.test.sh
acceptance.negativeControl: HoldPort mutated to release before Start fails its regression; a non-socket fd exits 1 naming the variable; occupied overrides fail with address already in use

acceptance.criterion: A2: four parallel copies of go test -count=1 -tags natslive ./core/ ./seed/ pass, three rounds in a row
acceptance.surface: GitHub runner: push-triggered proof workflow on branch infra-253/parallel-proof, pinned to the code-head SHA; 12 logs uploaded

acceptance.surface: PR CI at the head; pod with Job Postgres or the proof workflow's pgvector job

acceptance.surface: pr-and-main test job and its Stage 1 live proof (with the /proc inode-holder check); envoy-and-contracts dispatch job; docs.yaml docs:media; the pod for the claude-envoy smoke; devbox session 01a16962-c84b-7015-9e1d-64beb0a67775 via the tester for the devbox-only scripts

decisions: Architect: the added sites are in this PR, as one PR in phases; the stage4a/4b ports 13372/13373 stay unchanged because the devbox security group pins them; LEGION_LISTEN_FD, the keeper for same-port restarts, --max-time 5 on stage3's down-check, and the bridge-tunnel port-forward-on-0 design with a chisel restart are accepted; the host wrapper image is accepted with no spec departure.
Planner: an inherited socket is checked against only the settings that are set, by IP equality; listener PORT=0 with a descriptor is refused; DISPATCH_SERVER_URL is never derived from the socket.

Planner: shell harnesses use scripts/e2e/lib/held-port.py (exec and keep); e2e-local and the claude-envoy smoke use port 0 and report; the Playwright suite starts through e2e/run.ts so its config evaluates after the ports are discovered.
Planner: no positive explicit-override run is added for e2e-local, because it would need a released port; the occupied-override refusals prove an override is used as given.

findings.finding: The listener's inherited-socket path can bypass its existing non-loopback authentication fence unless authentication uses the socket's actual address. The draft adopts the socket at main.go:547–551, after the authentication check. Its explicit-setting mismatch rule does not cover an omitted ENVOY_LISTEN_HOST: config.Load supplies 127.0.0.1, so an inherited wildcard socket could otherwise pass as loopback.
findings.answer: Plan 1c: with ENVOY_LISTEN_FD, Inspect/CheckAgainst run before the auth fence, and cfg.ListenHost becomes the socket's IP. An inherited 0.0.0.0 socket without credentials is refused. Real-binary tests in cmd/listener (envoy-go) cover a wildcard without credentials, loopback without credentials, and a PORT mismatch.

findings.finding: The proposed Pulumi implementation contradicts the repository's explicit rule that live tests do not build their own image, and the wrapper image cannot replace the ordinary smoke image indiscriminately.
findings.answer: Plan 2.5: a separate envoy-smoke workflow step builds the wrapper and the derived image legion-envoy-smoke-heldport (FROM the smoke image; the real binary moves to /usr/local/libexec, and USER and entrypoint stay). ENVOY_SMOKE_HELD_PORT_IMAGE goes through pulumitest.HeldPortImage, and no test builds an image. internal/smoke keeps ENVOY_SMOKE_IMAGE.

findings.finding: The descriptor handoff has multiple independently owned descriptors, not the single 'test's own copy' described by the draft. Closing only one leaves the port held after the child exits; closing the last parent copy too early restores the race. Opening a listener inside resolveBootConfig also introduces ownership on its later error returns and on direct test callers.
findings.answer: Plan 1a/1e: Inspect takes no ownership, and Adopt always closes the raw fd. Dispatch inspects in resolveBootConfig and adopts at the bind site, so the direct resolveBootConfig callers own nothing. cmdtest.HoldPort closes its net.Listener after File(). Start closes ExtraFiles after cmd.Start, and Cleanup closes the File. The regression test covers: a competing bind is refused before the child serves, the child serves, and the port is released after the child exits.

findings.finding: The draft does not distinguish the opposite CLOEXEC requirements at the wrapper boundary and inside the final server. The handoff descriptor must survive the Python/Go wrapper's exec, but must not leak into unrelated descendants of the server.
findings.answer: Plan 1a: the raw fd is closed after FileListener, and the serving copy is close-on-exec (fcntl asserts). held-port.py dup2s to 3 as inheritable, handling the case where it is already 3. Real-process descendant checks (/proc fd and fdinfo) run on both wrapper paths: held-port.test.ts with the real envoy-listener, heldportwrapper/main_test.go, and the stage1 inode-holder check. Failure release is tested.

findings.finding: FileListener plus a TCP type assertion does not establish the promised 'already listening TCP socket' contract. A connected or merely bound TCP socket can be wrapped as a TCPListener without the intended startup refusal.
findings.answer: Plan 1a: Inspect checks SO_TYPE stream, the inet family and SO_ACCEPTCONN. It has a refusal matrix (malformed, 0-2, closed, file, pipe, UDP, unix, connected TCP, bound-not-listening TCP), and each refusal names the variable with no fallback. Real-binary refusals for both binaries.

findings.finding: The address-agreement rule needs an explicit effective-address contract. Comparing resolved defaults would reject valid inherited-only use, while string equality would mishandle existing IPv6 spellings. Socket address and public browser origin must remain separate concepts.
findings.answer: Plan 1a CheckAgainst: only set settings are compared, by IP equality with brackets allowed; wildcards match only the unspecified address; v4 and v6 never match; a hostname is refused. Listener PORT=0 with a descriptor is refused (decision). DISPATCH_PORT=0 stays refused. DISPATCH_SERVER_URL is independent and not derived. Dev sign-in judges the real socket address. The natslive dispatch permissions test exercises sign-in on the held port.

findings.finding: The host wrapper introduces a new, currently unexercised restart/handoff mechanism. A healthy first start alone does not establish that it works for the unseeded restart loop or preserves adoption and destruction behavior.
findings.answer: Plan 2.5: the test holds the socket and serves @legion-envoy-held-port-<port>, handing a dup to every connection. Its cleanup is registered before NewStack, so it runs after destroy. Programs A and B use the same port and image. The provider, health, destroy, adoption and unseeded assertions stay. A docker restart check is added. A negative control uses the plain image. The wrapper exits 1 on failure, naming the socket.

findings.finding: The probe-script two-address rewrite is incomplete unless it preserves independent task failure semantics. Moving both fakes into one Python process makes the existing exiting mode kill the healthy peer, and binding only one OS-selected address does not reserve the pair.
findings.answer: Plan 2.6: one Python process per case reserves both addresses, retries only on a second-bind EADDRINUSE with both closed, and writes a fresh port file once ready. Each address has its own mode and counter thread. exiting closes only its own socket. A no-server address is bound but not listening. The fake Dispatch binds 0 per start. The retry path is proved in a throwaway run.

findings.finding: The e2e-local change reaches URL construction, process-owned readiness, lock/signal tests and operator docs—not just the three launch arguments. The draft's claim that the second refusal run 'now gets OS ports' is inaccurate: it must not bind anything.
findings.answer: Plan 2.6: e2e-local builds each URL only after its process reports (natsd -p -1 log, listener JSON .addr, Bun ready line), and the readonly declarations move after the reports. Overrides are used as given. Occupied-override refusals are added for E2E_PORT and E2E_SESSION_PORT. The fixed overrides at :106 are dropped (the run is refused on the lock before binding). The lock, markers and TERM behaviour are preserved. Docs updated.

findings.finding: The binaries' new public settings are absent from the draft's documentation and settings-coverage tasks. Dispatch cannot read a new variable ad hoc without violating its existing single-settings-table contract.
findings.answer: Plan 1b-1d: a DISPATCH_LISTEN_FD settings row with its TestEverySettingReachesItsReader case; the generated reference regenerated from the table; dispatch README; the listener deploy README table, saying a container cannot take a host fd; LEGION_LISTEN_FD in AGENTS.md and docs/deployment.md; packages/envoy and claude-envoy CHANGELOGs.

findings.finding: The Go migration needs a consistent launcher API that preserves production-renderer coverage. Merely replacing the listed integer allocations is insufficient for hub_host_live_test, whose config and requests must agree with the held socket. Several comments also become false when Dispatch adopts a socket before its signal handler.
findings.answer: Plan 2.4: startListenerConfig takes the HeldPort, and the callers set ListenerConfig.Port=held.Port and keep rendering through config.Env. The renderer's positive-port check is unchanged. Dispatch readiness still needs its own listening line plus a live process. The obsolete FreeTCPPort, late-bind and net.Listen comments are rewritten, and the wrong-process regression is kept.

findings.finding: Acceptance 1 has no decisive regression/negative-control plan. Deleting FreeTCPPort and obtaining green suites would not show that the replacement never releases the socket between allocation and serving, nor that explicit overrides and failure release still work.
findings.answer: Plan 1e and A1a/A1b: a deterministic regression where a competing bind is refused between Start and serve, with a negative control (the mutated helper releases before Start and fails). Invalid descriptors are refused with no fallback. Occupied explicit overrides are refused. The host test keeps its reservation until teardown. A structural grep complements these checks.

findings.finding: Acceptance 2 still lacks an executable runner entry point and evidence collection. The existing workflow cannot be dispatched or triggered by a normal scratch-branch push as-is, and a bare wait over parallel jobs can hide an individual failure.
findings.answer: Plan section 5 proof workflow: the scratch branch infra-253/parallel-proof has a push-triggered workflow pinned to the code-head SHA. It runs setup-go and pull-test-images, then the A2 loop with a separate log and PID per copy, waits on every PID and fails on any nonzero exit. The 12 logs are uploaded and the run id and SHA recorded. The branch is deleted afterwards.

findings.finding: The verification-surface claim that memory/multiprocess 'need a GitHub runner' is unsupported by the code. They need Postgres, not Docker in the test process. The Kubernetes fallback statements also conflate a database workload with a Docker-backed natslive/pulumilive runner.
findings.answer: Corrected. The PR CI jobs are the mandatory surfaces. memory, multiprocess, dispatch and daemon tests run in the pod against a Kubernetes Job Postgres, after the documented can-i create jobs, create services and get services gate. Only natslive, pulumilive and A2 need a Docker GitHub runner. Each proof records its surface, and a skipped test is never reported as exercised.

findings.finding: Acceptance 3 names jobs and manual scripts, but the draft does not yet specify all script invocations or a real-process negative control for the new Python launcher. Its correctness also includes PID/exec and cleanup behavior, not just writing a port file.
findings.answer: Plan 2.6: held-port.py execs in place, so $! is the server's PID. The port file is written only after the socket listens. A failed exec releases the port. The A3b commands are named for search-smoke and for both searchbench query sets. The negative control is --binary /bin/false, which exits promptly with nothing left. No MRR threshold is invented.

specDepartures.spec: The spec's Problem list and Acceptance name the Envoy tests and test scripts in packages/envoy and their CI jobs, and its fix touches envoy-dispatch and envoy-listener.
specDepartures.plan: The plan also changes the Legion daemon (LEGION_LISTEN_FD for legion start, and a boot log naming the bound address), the daemon's scratch-Dispatch test, the claude-envoy smoke script, the whole Dispatch Playwright harness (with a new e2e/run.ts entry point), every scripts/e2e stage proof and rig.sh user, and deletes scripts/e2e/lib/free-port.sh. The stage4a/4b security-group-pinned ports 13372/13373 stay unchanged.
specDepartures.evidence: Scouts found boundPort (daemon_test.go:243), smoke-session-title.sh free_port (:73-80), run-server.sh fixed defaults (:21-24) and free-port.sh with its rig.sh callers. The daemon refuses port 0 (config.go:861) and has no inherited-socket path. The architect put these sites in this PR under the standing ruling dispatch://INFRA-49/ask/2d080aec-ce9a-4c7c-a235-ae998d2b0830, and said they need no spec edit.

outcome.scope: The scope grows beyond packages/envoy to packages/daemon, packages/dispatch/e2e, packages/claude-envoy, packages/pi-legion's skill-scenarios rig, docs/site/media and scripts/e2e. The spec's Acceptance holds as written and is applied to these sites too. The architect decided no spec edit is needed.
